cards.explanation: The answer is disaster from the north, friends. The LORD says disaster looms from the north, even great destruction (Jeremiah 6:1). That's why He says to sound the ram's horn in Tekoa and send up a signal over Beth-haccherem. I think a warning like that is meant to get attention.

The answer is False. The LORD says, “Though she is beautiful and delicate, I will destroy the Daughter of Zion” (Jeremiah 6:2). Notice that little word “Though,” friends. Being called beautiful doesn't turn into a free pass here.

The new plan is to attack by night, friends. The attackers say, “Rise up, let us attack by night and destroy her fortresses!” (Jeremiah 6:5). They had talked about noon, but now the daylight is fading and the evening shadows grow long (Jeremiah 6:4). So the night becomes their new moment to strike.

The word is punished, friends. The LORD says, “This city must be punished; there is nothing but oppression in her midst” (Jeremiah 6:6). He gives the reason right there in the same breath. It's a serious line, so I'll let it stand.

The answer is True. The LORD says, “Violence and destruction resound in her; sickness and wounds are ever before Me” (Jeremiah 6:7). He sees all of it. I think this is a heavy verse, so it's okay to just sit with it.

The answer is that He will turn away and make her a desolation, friends. The LORD says, “Be forewarned, O Jerusalem, or I will turn away from you; I will make you a desolation, a land without inhabitant” (Jeremiah 6:8). Notice it starts with a warning. He says it ahead of time, before any of it happens.

The answer is True. The LORD says, “Pass your hand once more like a grape gatherer over the branches” (Jeremiah 6:9). Picture someone checking every branch one more time, friends. The words “once more” tell us it's a second pass.

The word is offensive, friends. The speaker says, “Look, their ears are closed, so they cannot hear. See, the word of the LORD has become offensive to them; they find no pleasure in it.” The speaker asks, “To whom can I give this warning? Who will listen to me?” (Jeremiah 6:10). That's a lonely spot to stand in.

The answer is False. The LORD says, “For both husband and wife will be captured, the old and the very old alike” (Jeremiah 6:11). The old and the very old are named with everybody else, friends. It's a heavy verse, so I'm keeping my jokes in the pantry.

The answer is that their houses are turned over to others, friends. The LORD says, “Their houses will be turned over to others, their fields and wives as well, for I will stretch out My hand against the inhabitants of the land…” (Jeremiah 6:12). Houses, fields and wives are all named together. The hand He stretches out is the reason.

The answer is deceit, friends. The LORD says, “For from the least of them to the greatest, all are greedy for gain; from prophet to priest, all practice deceit” (Jeremiah 6:13). He names the prophets and priests right alongside everyone else, from the least to the greatest.

The answer is “Peace, peace,” friends. The LORD says, “They dress the wound of My people with very little care, saying, ‘Peace, peace,’ when there is no peace at all” (Jeremiah 6:14). It's like saying “it's fine, it's fine” while the oven smokes. The words sound calm, but the LORD says the peace isn't there.

The word is blush, friends. The LORD says, “No, they have no shame at all; they do not even know how to blush” (Jeremiah 6:15). Blushing is what a face does when it feels ashamed. He says they don't even know how to do that.
